Performance: Getting more out of your training: strength, power and how well you recover between sessions. Pick it if training results are what you’re after.
Energy: Feeling steady through the day rather than flat by mid-afternoon. Pick it if the slump is what you want to change.
Sleep & recovery: Winding down, sleeping well and feeling rested. Pick it if nights and mornings are where you want things to be better.
Focus: Staying sharp and switched on, at work or anywhere else. Pick it if concentration is what you want more of.
Healthy ageing: Keeping moving well for the long run — joints, bones and the everyday basics. Choosing it also offers comfort mode and asks about stiff or sore spots.
All-round health: Covering the everyday basics, without one goal leading. Pick it if you just want the essentials done properly.
How hard sessions feel: Easy is chatting pace. Steady is working but comfortable. Flat out is hard to talk through. It helps size the recovery side of a stack.

What counts as daylight?: Being outdoors in daylight for twenty minutes or more at a time, with your face and arms uncovered: a walk, the school run, a lunch break outside, working outdoors. Through a window or in the car doesn’t count. It’s one of the things the stack engine weighs.

The circuit check: A few fixed safety questions before anything is suggested. They rule products out, never in, and nothing from them is ever sent to AI. Some answers mean a stack isn’t right, and it says so.

Weight loss: Losing fat while keeping your strength, with or without a weight-loss jab. If you use injections or tablets you can say so, and it stays private: it’s confirmed in the safety check and never sent to AI.
Oily fish: Salmon, mackerel, sardines, trout, herring and fresh tuna. Tinned tuna doesn’t count here. The plate is asked about so the stack fills gaps rather than doubling up on what you already eat.
What counts as a cup: A mug of coffee, a cup of tea, or a can of energy drink each count as one. Decaf and herbal teas don’t. It’s asked so the stack never adds caffeine on top of plenty.
Pre-workout: A powder or shot taken before training, usually with caffeine in it. Telling Amp you take one means nothing else with caffeine is suggested.
How you sleep: Great is waking up rested most days. OK is fine but not brilliant. Restless is waking in the night or rarely feeling rested. It’s about a normal week, not your best night.
Stiff or sore spots: Anywhere that often feels stiff or achy after training or first thing in the morning. It isn’t a diagnosis, and anything sharp, new or worsening is one for your GP.
Comfort mode: Bigger text, bigger buttons and no dragging. The questions are the same; only the way you answer them changes.

Which gift you get is chosen from the products we’re giving away at the time, to suit your answers. You can’t swap it for cash or for another product.
The gift doesn’t combine with a discount code. You get whichever is worth more on your order, and your receipt says which.
On a subscription, the gift comes in your first box only. Later boxes don’t include it.

If you return part of your stack and what you keep is under the minimum spend, you keep the gift; we don’t charge you for it.
We can end or change the free gift at any time. That never affects an order you’ve already placed.
